nodes.summary: Let $T$ be an alphabet with decidable equality and a primitive recursive encoding into the natural numbers. The predicate on encoded context-free grammars $g$ over $T$ that holds exactly when the language of $g$ is empty is a computable predicate.
nodes.title: Emptiness of context-free grammars is computable

nodes.summary: Let $T$ be an alphabet and $N$ a set of nonterminals, and let $V$ assign a language over $T$ to each nonterminal. A sentential form $X_1 \cdots X_m$ over $T$ and $N$ denotes under $V$ the concatenation $L_1 \cdots L_m$, where $L_t = V(X_t)$ if $X_t$ is a nonterminal and $L_t = \{X_t\}$ if $X_t$ is a terminal; the empty form denotes $\{\varepsilon\}$. Let $A \in N$ with $V(A) = \emptyset$. Then every sentential form…
nodes.title: A sentential form containing an empty nonterminal denotes the empty language

nodes.summary: In a context-free grammar $G$, if every nonterminal occurring in a sentential form $u$ derives some terminal word, then $u$ derives some terminal word.
nodes.title: Sentential forms of productive nonterminals derive terminal words

nodes.summary: Let $g$ be an encoded context-free grammar. A round sends a list $H$ of nonterminals to the left-hand sides of those productions of $g$ in whose right-hand side every nonterminal belongs to $H$. For every $k \ge 0$, every nonterminal obtained after $k$ rounds starting from the empty list derives some terminal word in the context-free grammar that $g$ denotes.
nodes.title: Soundness of the productive-nonterminal iteration

nodes.summary: Let $g$ be an encoded context-free grammar, let $L$ be the largest of $2$ and the lengths of the right-hand sides of the productions of $g$, let $K$ be the number of distinct left-hand sides of these productions, and let $N = L^{K+1}$ be the pumping bound of $g$. For every word $w$ in the language of $g$ with $|w| \ge N$, there is a word $v$ in the language of $g$ with $N \le |v| < 2N$.
nodes.title: Context-free pumping down below twice the pumping bound

nodes.summary: Let $w$ be a word and $i \le j \le |w|$, and write $w[i, j)$ for the factor of $w$ from position $i$ to position $j$. If $w[i, j) = uv$, then $i + |u| \le j$, $w[i, i + |u|) = u$ and $w[i + |u|, j) = v$.
nodes.title: Splitting a factor

nodes.summary: For a word $w = w_0 w_1 \cdots w_{n-1}$ and natural numbers $i$ and $j$, the factor of $w$ from position $i$ to position $j$ is obtained by dropping the first $i$ letters of $w$ and keeping at most the first $j - i$ letters of the rest, where $j - i$ is $0$ when $j \le i$. For $i \le j \le n$ it is $w_i w_{i+1} \cdots w_{j-1}$.
nodes.title: Factor of a word

nodes.summary: Let $g$ be an encoded context-free grammar and $w = w_0 \cdots w_{n-1}$ a word. An item is a triple $(A, i, j)$ of natural numbers, coded as a natural number by nested pairing. A round sends a list $R$ of items to the items $(A, i, j)$ such that $A \to X_1 \cdots X_m$ is a production of $g$, $j \le n$, and there are positions $i = k_0, k_1, \ldots, k_m = j$, each at most $n$, such that for every $t$ with…
nodes.title: Items found by the membership procedure

nodes.summary: For an encoded grammar $g$, one more round of the generating-nonterminal computation, applied to the productions of $g$ and the generating nonterminals of $g$, yields only generating nonterminals of $g$: every left-hand side of a production of $g$ whose right-hand side has all its nonterminals among the generating nonterminals of $g$ is itself a generating nonterminal of $g$.
nodes.title: The generating nonterminals are closed under one more round

nodes.summary: Let a list of productions be given, each a pair of a nonterminal $A \in \mathbb{N}$ and a right-hand side made of nonterminals and terminals, together with a list $G$ of nonterminals. One round returns, in order, the left-hand sides of those productions in whose right-hand side every nonterminal belongs to $G$.
nodes.title: One round of the generating-nonterminal computation

nodes.summary: For an encoded grammar $g$, start from the empty list of nonterminals and, in each round, replace the current list $G$ by the list of left-hand sides of those productions of $g$ whose right-hand sides contain no nonterminal outside $G$. The generating nonterminals of $g$ are the list obtained after as many rounds as $g$ has productions.
nodes.title: Generating nonterminals

nodes.summary: For every encoded context-free grammar $g$, the infiniteness test returns true on $g$ if and only if the language of $g$ is infinite.
nodes.title: Correctness of the infiniteness test

nodes.summary: Let $g$ be an encoded grammar and $N$ its pumping bound. The test returns true exactly when some word $w$ whose letters all occur as terminals in the productions of $g$, with $N \le |w| < 2N$, is accepted by the membership test for $g$.
nodes.title: The infiniteness test

nodes.summary: If the language of an encoded grammar $g$ contains a word whose length is at least the pumping bound of $g$, then the language of $g$ is infinite.
nodes.title: Long words make a context-free language infinite

nodes.summary: For every encoded context-free grammar $g$, the emptiness test returns true on $g$ if and only if the language of $g$ is empty.
nodes.title: Correctness of the emptiness test

nodes.summary: For an encoded grammar $g$, the test returns true exactly when the start nonterminal of $g$ is not among the generating nonterminals of $g$.
nodes.title: The emptiness test for context-free grammars

nodes.summary: For an encoded grammar $g$ and a word $w$, the candidate items are the triples $(A, i, j)$, encoded as natural numbers by pairing, where $A$ is the left-hand side of a production of $g$ and $i, j \le |w|$; each triple is listed once for every production whose left-hand side is $A$.
nodes.title: Candidate items for membership

nodes.summary: For an encoded grammar $g$, the length bound is the maximum of $2$ and the lengths of the right-hand sides of the productions of $g$.
nodes.title: Right-hand side length bound

nodes.summary: For every encoded context-free grammar $g$ and every word $w$, the membership test returns true on $g$ and $w$ if and only if $w$ belongs to the language of $g$.
nodes.title: Correctness of the membership test

nodes.summary: For an encoded grammar $g$ with start nonterminal $S$ and a word $w$, the test returns true exactly when the item $(S, 0, |w|)$ is among the items found for $g$ and $w$.
nodes.title: The membership test for context-free grammars

nodes.summary: Let $g$ be an encoded context-free grammar over an alphabet $T$ with decidable equality, let $w$ be a word over $T$, and let $\rho$ be an encoded right-hand side whose decoding yields a word $u$ in the grammar that $g$ denotes. If $i \le j \le |w|$ and $u$ is the factor of $w$ from position $i$ to position $j$, then $i$ is a start position of $\rho$ at $j$ for the word $w$ and the list of items found by the…
nodes.title: Completeness of the start positions

nodes.summary: Write $\langle s, t \rangle$ for the pairing bijection $\mathbb{N} \times \mathbb{N} \to \mathbb{N}$ given by $\langle s, t \rangle = t^2 + s$ if $s < t$ and $\langle s, t \rangle = s^2 + s + t$ otherwise. Given an encoded grammar $g$, a word $w$ and a list $R$ of items found so far, the round lists, for every production $A \to \rho$ of $g$, every position $j \le |w|$ and every start $i$ of $\rho$ for the factor of…
nodes.title: One round of the membership procedure

nodes.summary: If a word $w$ is generated by an encoded grammar $g$, then every letter of $w$ is among the terminals of $g$, that is, it occurs in the right-hand side of some production of $g$.
nodes.title: Letters of generated words occur in the productions

nodes.summary: For an encoded grammar $g$, let $L$ be the length bound of $g$, the larger of $2$ and the largest length of a right-hand side of a production of $g$, and let $K$ be the number of distinct left-hand sides of the productions of $g$. The pumping bound of $g$ is $L^{K+1}$.
nodes.title: Pumping bound of an encoded grammar

nodes.summary: Let $g$ be an encoded grammar with pumping bound $N$. Every word $w$ generated by $g$ with $|w| \ge N$ can be written as $w = uvxyz$ with $vy$ nonempty and $|vxy| \le N$, such that $u v^i x y^i z$ is generated by $g$ for every natural number $i$, including $i = 0$.
nodes.title: Pumping lemma for encoded grammars

nodes.summary: Given a list $G$ of nonterminals (natural numbers), the test accepts an encoded production $(A, \rho)$ when every symbol of $\rho$ is acceptable: a terminal always is, and a nonterminal is when it belongs to $G$. So the production is accepted exactly when every nonterminal occurring in $\rho$ belongs to $G$.
nodes.title: Acceptable productions

nodes.summary: Write $\langle s, t \rangle$ for the pairing bijection $\mathbb{N} \times \mathbb{N} \to \mathbb{N}$ given by $\langle s, t \rangle = t^2 + s$ if $s < t$ and $\langle s, t \rangle = s^2 + s + t$ otherwise. Given an encoded grammar $g$ and a word $w$, a natural number $x$ is a sound item when $x = \langle A, \langle i, j \rangle \rangle$ for some $A$, $i$, $j$ with $i \le j \le |w|$ such that the nonterminal $A$…
nodes.title: Sound items

nodes.summary: If an encoded grammar $g$ generates some word $w$, then the start nonterminal of $g$ is among the generating nonterminals of $g$ computed by the emptiness procedure.
nodes.title: Completeness of the generating-nonterminal computation

nodes.summary: Write $\langle s, t \rangle$ for the pairing bijection $\mathbb{N} \times \mathbb{N} \to \mathbb{N}$ given by $\langle s, t \rangle = t^2 + s$ if $s < t$ and $\langle s, t \rangle = s^2 + s + t$ otherwise. Given a word $w$, a list $R$ of items (natural numbers), a position $j$ and an encoded right-hand side $X_1 \cdots X_m$, a position $i$ is a start when there are positions $i = p_0, p_1, \ldots, p_m = j$ with…
nodes.title: Start positions of a right-hand side

nodes.summary: Write $\langle s, t \rangle$ for the pairing bijection $\mathbb{N} \times \mathbb{N} \to \mathbb{N}$ given by $\langle s, t \rangle = t^2 + s$ if $s < t$ and $\langle s, t \rangle = s^2 + s + t$ otherwise. Given a word $w$, a list $R$ of items, a list $S$ of positions and an encoded symbol $X$, the test at a position $i$ succeeds when either $X$ is a terminal $a$, $i + 1 \in S$ and the letter of $w$ at position $i$…
nodes.title: Fitting a symbol at a position

nodes.summary: Given a list $G$ of natural numbers and a symbol $s$ of an encoded grammar over an alphabet $T$, which is either a nonterminal $i \in \mathbb{N}$ or a terminal in $T$, $s$ is acceptable when it is a terminal or a nonterminal that occurs in $G$. The test returns a Boolean.
nodes.title: Acceptable symbols

nodes.summary: For an encoded context-free grammar $g$ over an alphabet $T$ with decidable equality, the list of the terminals that occur in the right-hand sides of the productions of $g$, each listed once.
nodes.title: The terminals of an encoded grammar

nodes.summary: For every alphabet $T$ with decidable equality and a primitive recursive encoding, the property of an encoded context-free grammar $g$ over $T$ that the language of $g$ is empty is decidable by a multi-stack machine. This is Sipser, Theorem 4.8: the problem $E_{\mathrm{CFG}}$ is decidable.
nodes.title: Emptiness of context-free grammars is decidable

nodes.summary: For every alphabet $T$ with decidable equality and a primitive recursive encoding, the property of an encoded context-free grammar $g$ over $T$ that the language of $g$ is infinite is decidable by a multi-stack machine. This is the problem $\mathrm{INFINITE}_{\mathrm{CFG}}$.
nodes.title: Infiniteness of context-free languages is decidable

nodes.summary: For every alphabet $T$ with decidable equality and a primitive recursive encoding, the property of a pair $(g, w)$, where $g$ is an encoded context-free grammar over $T$ and $w$ is a word over $T$, that $w$ is in the language of $g$ is decidable by a multi-stack machine. This is Sipser, Theorem 4.7: the problem $A_{\mathrm{CFG}}$ is decidable.
nodes.title: Membership for context-free grammars is decidable

nodes.summary: For a list $A$ of letters and a natural number $n$, the list obtained from the list whose only entry is the empty word by $n$ rounds, each of which replaces every word $w$, in order, by the words $a w$ for the letters $a$ of $A$, in order. Its entries are exactly the words of length $n$ all of whose letters occur in $A$.
nodes.title: The words of a given length over a list of letters
Theory of Computation

can_prove.label: ready to prove
can_prove.meaning: Statement is in Lean and nothing it needs is blocked, so the proof can start.

can_state.label: ready to state
can_state.meaning: Everything its statement uses is in Lean, so the statement can be written in Lean.

conditional.label: conditionally proved
conditional.meaning: Proof compiles, but rests on an open statement without a recorded Lean proof.

fully_proved.label: fully proved
fully_proved.meaning: Proved, and every prerequisite is fully proved too.

inventory_checked.label: inventory checked
inventory_checked.meaning: Module inventory checked in full; it records inspection, not a mathematical proof.

inventory_pending.label: inventory pending
inventory_pending.meaning: Module inventory not yet checked in full; it records inspection, not a mathematical proof.

not_ready.label: not ready
not_ready.meaning: Needs more blueprint work before it can be attempted.

proved.label: proved
proved.meaning: Proof compiles, but something it rests on is not finished.

stated.label: statement formalized
stated.meaning: Statement is in Lean; the proof is not.
